claims.text: Creep resistance in CrMnFeCoNi HEA multilayer coatings is governed primarily by nanoscale incoherent or semi-coherent interfaces.
Nanoscale incoherent or semi-coherent interfaces block dislocation motion.
Interfacial dislocation pile-ups generate back-stress that inhibits further plastic deformation.
Slight compositional differences or thermal-treatment variations can be used to tune lattice parameters between CrMnFeCoNi HEA layers.
Layer thicknesses of approximately 20 nm and 100 nm provide a controlled comparison of interface spacing.
The proposed creep comparison is conducted at approximately 300°C under constant load and otherwise identical test conditions.
Interfaces provide sites for dislocation storage.
Dislocation storage at interfaces produces back-stress that delays or prevents dislocation transmission across layers.
Engineered incoherent interfaces repeatedly interrupt continuous slip paths under elevated-temperature applied stress.
Dislocation accumulation at interfaces reduces overall time-dependent plastic deformation.
Multilayer coatings with optimized interface incoherency and spacing will have significantly lower creep rates than monolithic CrMnFeCoNi coatings.
When interface spacing is too large, multilayer creep behavior may approach that of the monolithic coating.
When interfaces are too coherent, multilayer creep behavior may approach that of the monolithic coating.
The proposed interface-blocking mechanism applies near 300°C for layer thicknesses ranging from tens to roughly one hundred nanometers.
At much higher temperatures or with significantly thicker layers, other deformation mechanisms may dominate and diminish interface-barrier effectiveness.
The magnitude of creep-rate reduction and its sensitivity to interface spacing and incoherency are uncertain.
Failure of confirmed incoherent multilayers to reduce creep rate significantly relative to a monolithic control would falsify interface-mediated dislocation blocking as the predominant mechanism.
A creep rate independent of measured interface spacing and coherency would falsify the proposed predominant mechanism.
